item.research_question: Can a new high-entropy stannate pyrochlore oxide composition be synthesized via glycine-assisted sol–gel synthesis to form a single-phase structure suitable for thermal barrier coating applications, and what are its phase evolution, mechanical, and thermal expansion properties?
item.processing_route: Glycine-assisted sol–gel synthesis: metal oxides dissolved in HNO3 at 150 °C, SnCl2 and glycine (metal ions–glycine ratio 1:1.4 moles) added, heated to form gel/foam, calcined at 1000–1500 °C; pellets sintered at 1500 °C for 2 h then 5 h.
item.test_conditions: XRD (20–80°, 5°/min); FESEM (20 kV); Vickers hardness (500 g load, 10 s dwell); Dilatometry (25–900 °C, 5 °C/min heating rate in air).
key_findings: Single-phase pyrochlore oxide formed at calcination temperatures starting from 1300 °C without impurity or phase separation.
Mean particle size increased from 36 ± 5 nm (as-synthesized) to 884 ± 245 nm (1500 °C calcined).
Vickers hardness of the sintered high-entropy oxide was 4.2 ± 0.33 GPa.
Thermal expansion coefficient (TEC) calculated as 8.7 × 10−6 K−1 at 900 °C.
Lattice parameter for HEO-1500 was 10.5736 Å, lower than standard Pr2Sn2O7 (10.6004 Å).
Elemental mapping confirmed even distribution of all metal cations with no segregation in single-phase samples.
As-synthesized sample was completely amorphous; crystalline phases evolved with increasing calcination temperature.
item.mechanism: At lower temperatures, diffusion is sluggish and simpler oxides (e.g., Nd2O3, La2O3) form as secondary phases; higher temperatures provide adequate thermal energy for cation diffusion into the pyrochlore lattice, driven by the large negative −T△mixingS term in Gibbs free energy at high T. Pores formed during pressure-less sintering act as stress concentrators, reducing hardness.
item.limitations: The presence of pores in the sintered sample weakens mechanical properties and reduces hardness compared to traditional pyrochlores; one-step sintering at 1500 °C produced a brittle, non-dense pellet.
item.future_work: Optimization of sintering parameters and approaches, addition of sintering aids, and further exploration of complete functional applications as a thermal barrier coating material.
quotes: A single-phase pyrochlore oxide was formed from 1300 °C without any impurity or phase separation.
The mean particle size increases from 36 ± 5 nm to 884 ± 245 nm.
The calculated mean Vickers hardness of high-entropy stannate pyrochlore oxide is 4.2 ± 0.33 GPa.
